Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:1:1.hebrew: לרבות פחות כו' - ואת דריש, דכל אתין וגמין ריבויין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:1:1.english: To include less, etc. - [The baraita] expounds [the word] ve'et ["and that"], for all [instances of] etin [et] and gamin [gam] are [terms of] inclusion.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:2:1.english: If the court attends to the value of a peruta - [In a dispute] between a claimant and a defendant.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:2:2.hebrew: גומרין אפילו בפחות - אם חזר השני ותבעו פחות משוה פרוטה קודם שעמדו ב"ד משם, נזקקין לו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:2:2.english: [They] conclude [the case] even for less [than the value of a peruta] - If the second [party] came back and claimed from him less than the value of a peruta before the court rose from there, they attend to him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:1.english: One who eats terumah - [That is,] unintentionally; [it refers to] terumah gedolah.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:2.english: And terumah of the tithe - A tithe from the tithe.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:3.hebrew: ותרומת מעשר של דמאי - שהלוקח מעם הארץ צריך להפריש מספק, אבל תרומה גדולה של דמאי ליכא, דלא חייבוהו חכמים להפריש, כדאמרי' בסוטה (דף מח.): לפי ששלח בכל גבול ארץ ישראל וראה שלא היו מפרישין אלא תרומה גדולה בלבד, אלמא זהירין היו בה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:3.english: And teruma of the tithe of demai - For one who buys [produce] from an am ha'aretz [an unlearned person] must separate [teruma of the tithe] out of doubt; however, there is no teruma gedolah [great teruma] of demai, because the Sages did not obligate him to separate [it], as we say in Sotah (48a): because [Yochanan Kohen Gadol] sent [inspectors] throughout all the borders of the Land of Israel and saw that they were separating only teruma gedolah alone; thus, they were careful with it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:4.hebrew: מוסיף חומש - דכל הני איקרו תרומה: בתרומת מעשר כתיב (במדבר י״ח:כ״ו) "והרמותם ממנו תרומת ה'", בחלה כתיב (שם טו) "חלה תרימו תרומה", בבכורים כתיב (דברים י״ב:י״ז) "ותרומת ידך", ואמר מר: אלו בכורים (מכות דף יז.); וכל הני חד נינהו, דמשם אחד הן באין:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:4.english: He adds one-fifth - For all of these are called terumah: concerning terumah of the tithe it is written (Numbers 18:26), "And you shall set apart from it a terumah of the Lord"; concerning ḥalla it is written (ibid., 15[:20]), "ḥalla you shall set apart as terumah"; concerning first fruits it is written (Deuteronomy 12:17), "and the terumah of your hand," and the Master said: These are first fruits (Makkot 17a). And all of these are [considered] one [category], for they come from one name.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:5.hebrew: נטע רבעי - מוסיף חומש בפדיונו, דפדיון נטע רבעי "קדש" "קדש" גמר ממעשר בפ' שני דקדושין (דף נד:): גבי נטע רבעי כתיב "קדש הלולים", וגבי מעשר כתיב "כל מעשר הארץ מזרע הארץ וגו'". והני תרי נמי חד חשיב להו, דמחד קרא נפקי, דחומש בנטע רבעי לא כתיב, אלא ממעשר יליף:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:5.english: Fourth-year sapling - He adds one-fifth upon its redemption, for [the law of] redeeming a fourth-year sapling is derived from [second] tithe via [the verbal analogy of] "holy," "holy" in the second chapter of Kiddushin (54b): Regarding a fourth-year sapling it is written, "holy, for praising," and regarding tithe it is written, "All the tithe of the land, of the seed of the land, etc." And these two as well [the Mishnah] counts as one, because they are derived from one verse — for a fifth is not written regarding a fourth-year sapling, rather it is learned from tithe.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:6.hebrew: שלו - דוקא נקט, שאם חילל של אחרים אין מוסיף חומש. "איש ממעשרו" כתיב (ויקרא כז):
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:6.english: His [own] - [The Mishnah] stated [this] specifically, for if one redeemed [produce] belonging to others, he does not add a fifth. It is written, "a man [redeems] of his tithe" (Leviticus 27).

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:7.hebrew: הקדשו - ולא של אחרים, המקדיש כתיב:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:7.english: His consecrated [property] - And not [that] of others, [as] "the one who consecrates" is written.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:3:8.english: One who derives benefit - [That is,] unwittingly, for he is liable [to bring] a me'ilah [misappropriation] offering and [pay] a fifth.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:4:1.hebrew: קשיא ליה לר"א - משנתינו היתה קשה לר"א בן פדת:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:4:1.english: It was difficult for Rabbi Elazar - Our Mishnah was difficult for Rabbi Elazar ben Pedat.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:4:2.hebrew: עשו חכמים חיזוק - להוסיף על תרומת מעשר של דמאי חומש, שאין הפרשתו אלא מדבריהם:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:4:2.english: Did the Sages reinforce - to add a fifth onto teruma of the tithe of demai, whose separation is only by rabbinic decree.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:5:1.hebrew: המביא גט ממדינת הים - לאשה שעשאו בעלה שליח להוליכו לגרש, הצריכוהו לומר "בפני נכתב ונחתם". והתם מפרש: לפי שאין בקיאין לשמה, ואין עדים מצויין לקיימו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:5:1.english: One who brings a bill of divorce from a country overseas - to a woman whose husband made him an agent to bring it to divorce [her], [the Sages] required him to say, "It was written in my presence and it was signed in my presence." And there [in Tractate Gittin] it explains: because they are not expert [in writing it] for her sake, and witnesses are not readily available to validate it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:5:2.english: He must divorce [her] - The one who married her by means of this bill of divorce.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:7:1.english: One may desacralize it - [The mishna] teaches this regarding second tithe of demai.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:7:2.hebrew: נחושת על הפירות - ואפי' חוץ לירושלים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:7:2.english: Copper upon produce - And even outside of Jerusalem.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:7:3.hebrew: ויחזור ויפדה את הפירות - ויעלה הכסף לירושלים, דכתיב (דברים יד) וצרת הכסף:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:7:3.english: And he may then redeem the produce - And he shall bring the money up to Jerusalem, as it is written (Deuteronomy 14): "And you shall bind up the money."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:7:4.hebrew: וחכ"א יעלו פירות ויאכלו בירושלים - ולא הזקיקוהו לכך לחזור ולחללן, ואם רוצה מעלה הפירות עצמן, דהקילו בו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:7:4.english: And the Sages say: Produce shall be brought up and eaten in Jerusalem - They did not obligate him to do so — to desacralize them again — and if he wishes, he brings up the produce itself, for they were lenient with him.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:8:1.hebrew: ומי מחללינן כו' - מסקנא דתיובתא דאותיב רב ששת היא, והכי קאמר: שמענו לר"מ דמיקל בפדיון דמאי, לחללו כסף על כסף, כסף על נחושת; ובמעשר ודאי מי מחללינן כי האי גוונא, אפילו כסף על נחושת דדמי לפדיון? והתנן כו':
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:8:1.english: And can one desacralize, etc. - This is the conclusion of the refutation that Rav Sheshet raised, and this is what he is saying: We have heard concerning Rabbi Meir that he is lenient regarding the redemption of demai, to desacralize it silver upon silver [or] silver upon copper; but regarding definite ma'aser, do we desacralize in this manner — even silver upon copper, which resembles redemption? "But didn't we learn, etc."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:8:2.english: That were intermingled - And he wants to derive benefit from the non-sacred [one].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:8:3.hebrew: מביא בסלע מעות - נחושת — מביא בדמי סלע, ואומר כל מקום כו'; נמצאו שתיהן חולין והמעות מעשר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:8:3.english: He brings coins for a sela - [Of] copper; he brings [coins] for the value of a sela, and says, "Wherever..." etc. Thus both [sela coins] are found to be non-sacred, and the coins [become second] tithe.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:8:4.hebrew: ובורר את היפה שבהן - ומחלל עליה המעות הללו, ותהא היא מעשר, והמעות והסלע השני חולין כבראשונה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 55b:8:4.english: And he selects the better one among them - And he redeems these coins upon it, so that it becomes [second] tithe, while the coins and the second sela are non-sacred as before.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:4:1.hebrew: וכי עשו דבריהם כשל תורה - אע"ג דבכמה מקומות עשו אפי' יותר משל תורה, היינו היכא דשייך לקנוס כדי לעשות סייג; אבל הכא, אפילו בתרומת מעשר ודאי לא הוה שייך למקנס חומש אם לא שאמרה תורה, ולכך לא היה לקנוס בשל דמאי. ומשני דה"נ עשו הולד ממזר, אע"פ שאין סברא, אלא משום דבאשת איש הולד ממזר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:4:1.english: And did they make their pronouncements like those of the Torah? - Even though in several places they made [their pronouncements] even [more stringent] than those of the Torah, that is where it is relevant to impose a penalty in order to make a fence [around the law]; however, here, even for terumat ma'aser of definite [untithed produce], it would not be relevant to penalize [with] a fifth had the Torah not stated [it], and therefore it was not [appropriate] to penalize in [the case of] demai. And [the Gemara] answers that so too [in the case of a bill of divorce] they rendered the offspring a mamzer, even though there is no [logical] reason [for a penalty], except because in [the case of] a married woman [by Torah law] the offspring is a mamzer.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:5:1.hebrew: ולא אמר בפני נכתב ונחתם - נכתב לא נקט אלא משום רבנן, דלר"מ אין צריך לומר נכתב, דא"ר יהודה: אומר היה ר"מ, אפי' מצאו באשפה כשר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:5:1.english: And did not say, "In my presence it was written and signed" - [The baraita] only mentioned "it was written" because of the Rabbis, for according to Rabbi Meir one does not need to say "it was written," as Rabbi Yehuda said: Rabbi Meir used to say [that] even if he found it in a garbage heap, it is valid.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:5:2.hebrew: וחכמים אומרים אין הולד ממזר - מדלא קאמרי רבנן "לא תצא", דעדיפא טפי, מכלל דסבירא להו דתצא, אע"ג דאין הולד ממזר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:5:2.english: And the Sages say: The offspring is not a mamzer - Since the Rabbis do not say "she does not leave [her husband]," which would be a stronger [ruling], it follows by implication that they hold that she must leave [him], even though the offspring is not a mamzer.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:5:3.hebrew: כיצד יעשה - פירוש: לרבנן, כיצד יעשה אם ניסת שלא יצטרך להוציא; אי נמי לר"מ, כיצד יעשה קודם שניסת ולא יצטרך גט אחר, אבל אחר שניסת אין נראה לר"מ שיהיה שום תקנה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:5:3.english: How should [the agent] proceed? - Explanation: According to the Rabbis, [the baraita asks] how should he proceed if she remarried, so that [her husband] will not have to divorce [her]; or alternatively, according to Rabbi Meir, [it asks] how should he proceed before she remarried, so that [he] will not need another bill of divorce, but after she remarried, it does not appear [possible] according to Rabbi Meir that there would be any remedy.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:5:4.hebrew: יטלנו הימנה - וא"ת: ויאמר "בפני נכתב ונחתם" בעודנו בידה? וכי תימא צריך לומר קודם נתינה — האמר בפרק קמא דגיטין (דף ה. ושם): כגון שנתנו לה ולא הספיק לומר עד שנתחרש! ויש לומר דצריך לומר אחר נתינה מיד שנתגרשה, בעודם עסוקים באותו ענין:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:5:4.english: He should take it from her - And if you ask: Let him say, "It was written in my presence and signed [in my presence]," while it is still in her hand! And if you say [that] he must say [it] prior to giving [the bill of divorce] — did it not state in the first chapter of Gittin (5a and there): "[The case is] where he gave it to her and did not manage to say [it] before he became a deaf-mute"?! And one can answer that he must say [it] immediately after giving [it], when she is divorced, while they are still engaged in that same matter.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:7:1.hebrew: ויחזור ויפדה - פרש"י: כן צריך לעשות, דבעינן "וצרת הכסף בידך", וחכמים אומרים: אם ירצה, יעלה הפירות עצמן. ופריך, דבודאי אסור כסף על נחשת שלא מדוחק, והכא גבי דמאי שרי. וקשה לפירושו, דמכמה מקומות ה"מ לאתויי דמצינו דמאי קל מודאי: דבמסכת דמאי (פ"א מ"ב) תנן: "הדמאי אין לו חומש ואין לו ביעור", ובמתני' תנן נמי: "מעשר שני מוסיף חומש", ולא קתני "של דמאי", כדקתני גבי "האוכל תרומת מעשר"; ועל חנם הביא מתני' דדמאי ודמעשר שני. ותו, מדקאמר: "מדוחק אין, שלא מדוחק לא", משמע דשאר המשנה אתיא ליה שפיר; והלא עדיפא ה"מ למפרך, דכסף על כסף אסור בודאי אפי' מדוחק, מדלא מתנה על אחד מן הסלעין, ובדמאי שרי! ותו, מה שפירש דלפדות הפירות עדיף מלעלות — אפכא משמע בכמה דוכתי: בפ"ג דמעשר שני (מ"י) גבי "לקוח בכסף מעשר שני שנטמא כו'", "אמר להם: לא, אם אמרתם כו', תאמר בלקוח שאינו נפדה טהור ברחוק מקום" — אלמא לקוח צריך להעלותו; וכן בכמה דוכתי. לכן נראה לפרש, דלר"מ אם ירצה יחזור ויפדה הפירות, וחכ"א דצריך להעלותו. ופריך אמאי דשני שמואל, דר"מ מחמיר בדמאי יותר מחכמים, והכא מיקל טפי מחכמים. אבל הא לא קשיא ליה: אמאי מוסיף חומש בתרומת מעשר של דמאי כודאי, ובפדיון לא מחמיר? דדוקא באכילה שעושה עבירה מחמיר בדמאי כמו בודאי, אבל בפדיון שאינו עושה עבירה לא החמירו. והוצרך להביא מתניתין ד"מחללין כסף על נחשת מדוחק", דלא תימא כמו כן מיקל ר"מ בודאי, וא"כ משוה הוא דמאי לודאי כמו בתרומת מעשר; לכך מייתי דגבי ודאי אין מחללין כסף על נחשת שלא מדוחק, וא"כ קשה דהא מיקל בדמאי לגבי ודאי יותר מחכמים. ואביי ס"ל בסמוך, דשמא ר"מ מחמיר גבי מיתה בדמאי כודאי יותר מחכמים, וגבי לאו לא מחמיר כמו בודאי; ורבנן, אע"ג דמחמרי גבי לאו, גבי מיתה דתרומת מעשר של דמאי אין נראה להם לקנוס חומש, כדפ"ל, דאפילו בודאי לא היה לקנוס אם לא שצותה תורה. ומיהו קשה, דגרסינן במשנה במלתיה דר"מ: "ובלבד שיפדה הפירות". וי"ל: כך מחללין כסף על כסף — אפילו לחזור ולפדות אותו הכסף על דבר אחר; וכן נחשת על הפירות — דומיא כמו שפירש כסף על כסף. "ובלבד שיפדה" — פירוש: בלבד שיהא דעתו מתחילה, כשחלל נחשת על הפירות, לחזור ולפדות הפירות — אז מותר; אבל אם היה אז דעתו להעלותם, ונמלך לפדותן — צריך להעלותן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:7:1.english: And he may then redeem [the produce] - Rashi explained: Thus he is required to do, for we require "and you shall bind up the money in your hand" (Deuteronomy 14:25); and the Sages say: If he wishes, he may bring up the produce itself. And [Rav Sheshet] objects that in the case of definite [second tithe], [desacralizing] silver upon copper is forbidden when not under duress, whereas here regarding demai it is permitted. And [Rashi's] explanation is difficult: for from several places [Rav Sheshet] could have adduced that we find demai is more lenient than definite [tithe] — for in Tractate Demai (1:2) we learned: "Demai is not subject to the added fifth and is not subject to removal," and in our Mishnah we also learned: "Second tithe adds a fifth," and it does not teach "of demai," as it teaches regarding "one who eats terumat ma'aser [of demai]"; so in vain did [Rav Sheshet] cite the Mishnah of Demai and of Ma'aser Sheni! Furthermore, from [the Gemara's] statement, "Under duress, yes; not under duress, no," it is implied that the rest of the Mishnah fits well with his [objection]; yet could he not have raised a stronger objection, that [desacralizing] silver upon silver is forbidden in definite [second tithe] even under duress — since he does not stipulate regarding one of the selas — whereas in demai it is permitted? Furthermore, as to what [Rashi] explained, that redeeming the produce is preferable to bringing [it] up — the opposite is implied in several places: in the third chapter of Ma'aser Sheni (mishna 10), regarding "[produce] purchased with second-tithe money that became impure, etc.," "He said to them: No, if you say [so regarding...], etc., will you say [so] regarding [produce] purchased [with second-tithe money], which cannot be redeemed when pure in a distant place" — thus [produce] purchased [with second-tithe money] must be brought up [to Jerusalem]; and similarly in several places. Therefore, it seems [preferable] to explain that according to Rabbi Meir, if he wishes, he may go back and redeem the produce, whereas the Sages say that he must bring it up. And [Rav Sheshet] objects against what Shmuel answered — that Rabbi Meir is more stringent regarding demai than the Sages — whereas here he is more lenient than the Sages. However, this was not difficult to him: why does he add a fifth for terumat ma'aser of demai as [for] definite [tithe], while regarding redemption he is not stringent? Because specifically regarding eating, where one commits a transgression, he is stringent regarding demai as [for] definite [tithe], whereas regarding redemption, where one does not commit a transgression, they were not stringent. And he needed to cite the Mishnah of "one desacralizes silver upon copper under duress," so that you should not say that Rabbi Meir is similarly lenient regarding definite [tithe], and if so, he equates demai to definite [tithe] just as in terumat ma'aser; therefore he cites that regarding definite [tithe] one does not desacralize silver upon copper when not under duress, and if so, it is difficult, for he is more lenient regarding demai relative to definite [tithe] than the Sages. And Abaye holds shortly below that perhaps Rabbi Meir is stringent regarding [a prohibition punishable by] death [at the hand of Heaven] in demai as [for] definite [tithe] more than the Sages, whereas regarding a negative commandment he is not as stringent as [for] definite [tithe]; while the Rabbis, even though they are stringent regarding a negative commandment, regarding [the prohibition punishable by] death of terumat ma'aser of demai it does not seem [right] to them to penalize [with] a fifth, as I explained above, since even for definite [tithe] one would not penalize were it not that the Torah commanded [it]. However, it is difficult, for we read in the Mishnah in Rabbi Meir's statement: "provided that he redeems the produce." And one can answer: Thus one may desacralize silver upon silver — even to go back and redeem that silver upon something else; and similarly copper upon produce — just as it explained [regarding] silver upon silver. And "provided that he redeems" — meaning: provided that his intention from the outset, when he desacralized copper upon the produce, was to go back and redeem the produce — then it is permitted; but if his intention at that time was to bring them up, and he changed his mind to redeem them — he must bring them up.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:7:2.hebrew: כסף על נחשת - וא"ת כיון דתנא דמחללים כסף על כסף, אע"ג דאסור בודאי אפילו מדוחק, כ"ש כסף על נחשת דשרי, דאפי' בודאי מדוחק שרי כדאמר בסמוך? וי"ל: איידי דתנא נחשת על פירות, דפליגי בה רבי מאיר ורבנן, תנא נמי כסף על נחשת, דהוי נמי טבעא אפירא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 55b:7:2.english: Silver upon copper - And if you ask: Since [the Mishnah] taught that one may desacralize silver upon silver, even though it is forbidden for definite [second tithe] even in a pressing circumstance, all the more so [is it obvious] that silver upon copper is permitted, since for definite [second tithe] it is permitted in a pressing circumstance, as [the Gemara] says shortly? And one can answer: Since [the Mishnah] taught copper upon produce, regarding which Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis disagree, it also taught silver upon copper, for it is also [a case of] coin upon produce.
